PC: Ask for intravenous (IV) access, to have patient placed on monitor, call for nasal cannula
Manage PEA arrest per Advance Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) protocols
Perform CPR in 2-minute cycles with pulse/rhythm checks in between
Manage Vifb arrest per ACLS protocols
Ask for defibrillator and defibrillate patient
Continue CPR with pulse and rhythm checks every 2 minutes
Manage stable SVT per ACLS protocols
Consider vagal maneuvers (these may include carotid sinus massage, Valsalva maneuver)
Consider adenosine 6 mg intravenous.  May give second dose at 12 mg.
Discuss possible post-cardiac arrest care:This may include 12-lead EKG; lab work such as troponin, BMP, CBC; consider definitive airway such as intubation if patient was not neuro-intact
MK: Discuss reversible causes of PEA arrest:These can include Hypoxia, Acidosis, Hyperkalemia, Hypokalemia, Hypothermia, Tamponade, Tension pneumothorax, Coronary or pulmonary thrombosis, Toxins
ICS: The learner will take lead and assign clear roles
